title: App security updates: Thank you, plus what's required next
summary:
Thanks to you, we've already seen the vast majority of apps that run bulk operations adopt an IP allowlist. That's a big step toward keeping merchants protected heading into the busiest weeks of the year.

Here's what's required, what's new, and what's coming next.

Action required

  • All public apps that call the Admin API: Turn on an IP allowlist by November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Apps without one will be delisted from the Shopify App Store and blocked from new installs. Existing installs keep working. For apps that are delisted, we'll relist apps automatically once they add an IP allowlist. Set up your IP allowlist
  • Bulk operations: We're beginning enforcement on bulk queries and mutations from public apps without an IP allowlist. Turn on your allowlist to restore them.
  • Enable bulk operations for partner-created apps: Before your app can run bulk queries or bulk mutations, enable them from API access requests in the Partner Dashboard. If your app doesn't start a bulk query or mutation for 31 days, you'll need to enable it again. Read the changelog
  • Custom apps installed outside your organization also need an IP allowlist: These apps need an IP allowlist for new installs from November 20, 2026, and for existing installs from January 1, 2027. From January 1, one app without an allowlist blocks you from installing any of your apps on stores outside your organization. Apps installed only within your organization, and apps created by merchants, aren't affected. Read the changelog

New this week

  • You can now use IP addresses and ASNs together. Your allowlist can include IP addresses, CIDR ranges and your hosting provider's ASNs at the same time, with up to 250 IP addresses or ranges. A request is allowed if it matches any entry. Country restrictions apply only to ASNs. For the strongest protection, use specific IP addresses wherever you can. Read the changelog

Coming soon

  • MFA on every partner account. Starting next week, multi-factor authentication will be required on all partner accounts. We recommend passkeys. Turn on MFA now so it doesn't interrupt your work later. Protect the accounts that control your app

Get help

If you see something suspicious, tell us right away at partner-security-reports@shopify.com. You're responsible for fixing it and notifying affected merchants, and we'll support you through it.

For general security questions, contact Shopify Support.

Everything lives in the App Security Hub, and we answer questions on the App Security board in the developer community.

title: Market metafields break ties between equally specific markets by market handle
summary: When a buyer matches two or more equally specific markets that set the same metafield, Market.metafield and Market.metafields now return the value from the market with the lowest handle, instead of the value that was updated most recently. This behavior change applies to the Storefront API, Liquid, and Function APIs on every API version. If your app or theme reads market metafields on stores with overlapping markets, check which value buyers get in a tie.

title: Market.metafields matches keys in any case as of Storefront API version 2027-01
summary:
As of Storefront API version 2027-01, the metafields field on the Market object matches each requested key in any case, as Market.metafield already does. This is a breaking change for apps and custom storefronts that request a market metafield key in a different case from the stored key, or that read a key that the buyer's markets store that differ by letter case. If your app does either, review its Market.metafields queries before you move it to 2027-01.

What changed

In version 2027-01, Market.metafields returns a metafield when the requested key matches the stored key in any case. In earlier versions, Market.metafields returns a metafield only when the requested key and the stored key have the same case.

For example, a market stores a metafield with the namespace custom and the key colour:

  • In version 2026-10 and earlier, the entry for { namespace: "custom", key: "Colour" } is null.
  • In version 2027-01, the entry returns the stored metafield.

Who's affected

The change applies to apps and custom storefronts that query metafields on a Market object, from Localization.market or Country.market, with Storefront API version 2027-01 or later. Your app is affected only if one of these conditions is true:

  • It requests a key in a different case from the key that the market stores.
  • The buyer's markets store the same key in different cases.

Your app isn't affected if it requests each key in the case that the markets store it, or if it uses only Market.metafield, which already matches keys in any case. Versions 2026-10 and earlier don't change.

Why this matters

In earlier versions, Market.metafield and Market.metafields can return different results for the same key: Market.metafield finds the metafield, and Market.metafields returns null. In 2027-01, both fields return the same metafield, so your storefront shows the same value whichever field it queries.

What to do

Market.metafield already matches keys case-insensitively, and it returns the metafield from the buyer's most specific market. So on the version that you use today, Market.metafield returns the result that Market.metafields returns in 2027-01. You can compare the two fields to find out whether the change affects your app.

  1. For each market metafield that your app reads, query Market.metafield and Market.metafields with the same namespace and key, and compare the results.
  2. If the results are the same for every key, then you don't need to make changes.
  3. If a result is different, then check whether the difference has a material impact on your app or your storefront.
  4. If it does, then update your app and your metafields so that they don't depend on the case of keys. For example, request each key in the case that your markets store it, and use one case for each key on every market.
query CompareMarketMetafields @inContext(country: CA) {
  localization {
    market {
      metafield(namespace: "custom", key: "Colour") {
        key
        value
      }
      metafields(identifiers: [{ namespace: "custom", key: "Colour" }]) {
        key
        value
      }
    }
  }
}

Related docs

  • Market object in the Storefront API
  • Storefront API 2027-01 reference
  • Retrieve metafields with the Storefront API
  • About Shopify API versioning

title: Remove your app from the Shopify App Store yourself
summary:
You can now start sunsetting your app and remove it from the Shopify App Store yourself, from the Partner Dashboard. You no longer need to contact Shopify Support.

What's new

  • In the Partner Dashboard, go to Apps > your app > Distribution, and click Remove from App Store.
  • Choose a sunset date at least 30 days from now. This gives your merchants time to prepare and find an alternative.
  • Shopify removes your app from the Shopify App Store right away. Merchants can no longer find or install it there.

Removing your app from the Shopify App Store can't be undone. To list the app again, you need to submit it for review as a new app.

What happens to existing merchants

Removing your app from the Shopify App Store doesn't immediately affect merchants who already have it installed. They can keep using your app until your scheduled sunset date, when your app is sunset and removed from their stores.

Shopify doesn't email your merchants, cancel their charges, or uninstall your app for you. Before your sunset date, you're responsible for:

  • Telling your merchants about the sunset and reminding them before the sunset date
  • Cancelling app subscriptions with appSubscriptionCancel
  • Uninstalling your app from any remaining stores with appUninstall

Related docs

  • Sunsetting your app

title: IP allowlists are now required for custom apps installed outside your organization
summary:
We're enhancing protection of merchants by requiring IP allowlists for custom apps, if those apps are installed on stores outside of the organization that owns them.

  • Starting November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET: Apps must have an IP allowlist for new installs.
  • Starting January 1, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET: Allowlists are required for existing installs.

What apps are affected

  • Custom apps installed on stores outside the organization that owns the app.
  • Partners who own multiple apps. From January 1, 2027, one app without an allowlist affects your ability to install any app on stores outside your organization.

What apps are unaffected

  • Apps installed only on stores within your own organization
  • Apps created by merchants either in the Dev Dashboard or in the admin
  • Public apps, which are covered by a separate requirement

Why we're making this change

Leaked tokens can be used from any network location. IP allowlists reduce the impact of a credential leak by limiting the networks from which your app can invoke the Admin API.

What to do

Configure your app's allowed IPs in the Dev Dashboard:

  • If your app calls Shopify from static IP addresses, configure your IP allowlist based on static IPs or CIDR range.
  • If your app's egress IP addresses are dynamic, allow your hosting provider's ASNs and list the countries your app runs in.

Audit every app you've installed on stores outside your organization, and configure an allowlist on each one before January 1, 2027.

For setup instructions, see Restrict API access with an IP allowlist.

title: App IP allowlists now support IP addresses and ASNs together, and up to 250 IPs
summary:
Your app's IP allowlist in the Dev Dashboard can now include IP addresses and autonomous system numbers (ASNs) in the same allowlist. This helps apps whose requests come from a mix of static and dynamic IP addresses. You can also now configure up to 250 IP addresses or ranges, up from 100.

What changed

The IP allowlist section of your app's Settings page no longer makes you choose between IP addresses and networks. You can enter up to 250 addresses or ranges in IP addresses or CIDR ranges, up to 10 ASNs in Networks (ASN), or both. Under Limit ASNs to countries, you can choose up to 10 countries. Countries limit only your ASNs, not your IP addresses.

Requests are allowed if they match one of your configured IPs or ASNs. Requests from outside your allowlist fail with a 403 status code.

What to do

IP allowlists will soon be required for all public and custom apps. Shopify strongly recommends all apps use an IP allowlist.

Allow specific IP addresses wherever you can. This is the most secure option, because only your own servers can use your app's access tokens. An ASN allows every address on your hosting provider's network, including addresses used by the provider's other customers. Add ASNs only for requests that come from dynamic addresses, such as serverless functions, and limit them to the countries your app runs in.

Before you turn on enforcement, test your updated allowlist against recent traffic.

For setup instructions, see Restrict API access with an IP allowlist.

title: Storefront MCP policies and FAQs tool is being deprecated in favor of UCP MCP Ask tool
summary:
Storefront MCP search_shop_policies_and_faqs is deprecated. Migrate to UCP MCP's ask_business tool by January 15, 2027.

What's changing

The search_shop_policies_and_faqs tool on the Storefront MCP server (https://{shop}.myshopify.com/api/mcp) is deprecated in favor of the UCP Ask MCP tool.

UCP MCP implements the UCP ask capability (dev.ucp.common.ask) and exposes the following tool at the https://{shop-domain}/api/ucp/mcp endpoint:

  • ask_business: Answer a buyer's question about the store's policies and services, using the store's knowledge base and policies.

The deprecated tool will be maintained until January 15, 2027, but all documentation will refer to Ask MCP.

What you should do

If you're building with search_shop_policies_and_faqs:

  • Migrate calls to ask_business, and update endpoints to use https://{shop-domain}/api/ucp/mcp.
  • Include a meta object carrying ucp-agent.profile in every request. Your agent profile must declare dev.ucp.common.ask.
  • Send the question in ask.query, and optional buyer context (such as country or preferred language) in ask.context.
  • Note that ask_business returns a written answer in result.structuredContent.answer.plain, not raw knowledge base facts or full policy text. Update any code that parses the old response.
  • Use tools/list to check whether a store offers ask_business for your agent profile.

See the documentation for Ask MCP (https://shopify.dev/docs/agents/ask) for more details.

title: Customer data erasure requests updated from 10 days to 5
summary:
As of November 10, 2026, customer data erasure requests will no longer be held in a pending state for 10 days.

Erasure requests will now be processed 5 days after the request was submitted, regardless of when the customer's most recent order was placed. For recipients of gift cards that have been scheduled to send, the erasure request will remain in a pending state until the gift card has been delivered.

This update simplifies the overall experience for managing customer data requests.

title: Shopify App Store submission requirements: build, grow, then expand
summary:
We’re updating the Shopify App Store submission requirements so that the apps you list are apps merchants use. These changes apply to new app submissions, resubmissions of rejected apps, additional app listings, and listed apps with zero. They introduce new thresholds you must meet to submit and keep apps listed.

These policies apply to new submissions, resubmissions, and listed apps starting today.

What changed

We’ve updated the Shopify App Store submission and listing policies in four ways:

  • Minimum adoption before listing additional apps: Each of your existing apps must have at least 10 installs on full-priced Shopify stores before you can list an additional app. For details, see the submission limits in the App submission review guide.
  • Escalating cooldowns for rejected app submissions: Rejected submissions are subject to escalating cooldown periods before resubmitting. Cooldowns get longer with each repeated rejection, so resubmitting without meaningful changes leads to a longer wait. If a submission was rejected, make sure to address the review feedback before you resubmit so you don’t extend the cooldown period. For details, see the App submission paused section in App submission review and suspensions.
  • Identity verification for new apps: Identity verification is now a required step for developers who submit new apps so merchants know who’s behind the apps they install. You can complete identity verification from your partner account before you submit a new app.
  • Removal of apps with zero installs after six months: Apps with zero installs after six months are automatically removed from the Shopify App Store. For details, see the App usefulness check.

What you should do

Before submitting or resubmitting an app, confirm that you meet the applicable adoption and identity verification requirements and that any submission cooldown has ended.

For listed apps, review install counts to identify apps subject to automatic removal.

Who’s affected

These changes apply to you if any of the following are true:

  • You want to list an additional app in the Shopify App Store.
  • You’re resubmitting an app that was rejected in the Shopify App Store review.
  • You’re submitting a new app to the Shopify App Store.
  • You have an app listed in the Shopify App Store with no installs.

These changes don’t affect apps that already meet the install thresholds and remain installed on at least one full-priced Shopify store.

title: Redesigned Partner Directory with profiles built on Shopify data
summary:
The Shopify Partner Directory has been redesigned. We've made it easier for merchants to explore and evaluate Partners based on a definitive, Shopify-confirmed record of their work, while making profiles easier for Partners to maintain.

TL;DR:

  • Profiles are built largely from a Partner's collaboration and store transfer history over the past four years and are automatically updated as new work is completed.
  • Profile settings are now managed through Organization Settings.
  • Partners in Shopify’s Partner Program Select tier and above are eligible to be featured in the Partner Directory.
  • Reviews and ratings have been removed on profile pages.

What's new

Profiles are built largely from a Partner's collaboration and store transfer history over the past four years and are automatically updated as new work is completed.

Information displayed on profiles include the following:

Partner-controlled details

  • Business name, logo, and description
  • Contact information
  • Website and social links
  • Featured clients

Shopify-controlled data

  • Partner tier and tenure
  • Estimated company size
  • Estimated active projects
  • Top merchant industries supported
  • Top services provided
  • Top markets worked in

What do do

  1. Go to your profile in Organization Settings > Partner Program.
  2. Confirm that your business details, contact information, and links are up to date.
  3. [NEW] Choose your preferred contact destination and select up to 6 clients to feature

Related doc

event_model_payload.headline: Redesigned Partner Directory with profiles built on Shopify data
event_model_payload.summary:
The Shopify Partner Directory has been redesigned. We've made it easier for merchants to explore and evaluate Partners based on a definitive, Shopify-confirmed record of their work, while making profiles easier for Partners to maintain.

TL;DR:

  • Profiles are built largely from a Partner's collaboration and store transfer history over the past four years and are automatically updated as new work is completed.
  • Profile settings are now managed through Organization Settings.
  • Partners in Shopify’s Partner Program Select tier and above are eligible to be featured in the Partner Directory.
  • Reviews and ratings have been removed on profile pages.

What's new

Profiles are built largely from a Partner's collaboration and store transfer history over the past four years and are automatically updated as new work is completed.

Information displayed on profiles include the following:

Partner-controlled details

  • Business name, logo, and description
  • Contact information
  • Website and social links
  • Featured clients

Shopify-controlled data

  • Partner tier and tenure
  • Estimated company size
  • Estimated active projects
  • Top merchant industries supported
  • Top services provided
  • Top markets worked in

What do do

  1. Go to your profile in Organization Settings > Partner Program.
  2. Confirm that your business details, contact information, and links are up to date.
  3. [NEW] Choose your preferred contact destination and select up to 6 clients to feature

Related doc

Learn more in the Partner Directory profile help documentation.

title: Partner apps must enable bulk operations before use
summary:
Starting today, apps need access to bulk operations before they can run bulk queries or bulk mutations with the GraphQL Admin API. You can enable access for your app in the Partner Dashboard.

What changed

Bulk queries and bulk mutations are enabled separately:

  • To run bulkOperationRunQuery, your app needs access to bulk queries.
  • To run bulkOperationRunMutation, your app needs access to bulk mutations.

If your app starts a bulk operation without access, then the request returns an access denied error. The requirement applies to all GraphQL Admin API versions.

Who's affected

Public apps and custom apps that you build as a partner and that run bulk operations. Apps that merchants create in the Shopify admin or the Dev Dashboard aren't affected at this time.

If your app already runs bulk operations, then we've already enabled access for it. You can confirm this in the Partner Dashboard.

Apps that haven't run a bulk query or bulk mutation in the last 31 days lose access to that operation type. If your app loses access, then follow the steps below to enable it again.

What to do

Check your app's access and enable the operation types that it runs:

  1. From the Partner Dashboard, go to Apps, and then select your app.
  2. In the sidebar, click API access requests.
  3. Under Run bulk operations, click Allow bulk queries, Allow bulk mutations, or both. If an operation type is already enabled, then the section shows that it's enabled.

You don't need to change your app configuration, release a new app version, or ask merchants to reinstall your app. Access applies to every store that has your app installed.

For details, see Enabling access to bulk operations.

title: Dev Dashboard now shows when checkout and customer account UI extensions fail to load
summary:
When a UI extension fails to load, buyers don't see the experience you built, and the problem can be hard to spot from your side. The Dev Dashboard now shows these failures so you can find and fix them faster.

On your app's home page in the Dev Dashboard, the Operations section now includes:

  • Extension mount failure rate: how many times your extensions loaded and what share of those loads failed, over the date range you choose.
  • Top extension installations by failure rate: the stores and extension targets where the current version of your extensions fails most often. Installations with at least 10 loads are ranked, and each row links to that store's mount failure logs.

In Logs, a new UI extension event records each failed mount. You can filter these events by store, extension, target, and result.

Only failures caused by your app are counted. Failures that come from Shopify, the network, or the buyer's browser aren't included and don't show up in your logs.

Coming soon: merchant visibility and alerts

Merchants will soon see the same health information for the extensions installed on their store in Settings > Apps. The current version of each extension gets a status based on its last 7 days of loads:

  • Warning: we're confident that more than 5% of loads are failing, and it's lasted for 3 days.
  • Critical: we're confident that more than 50% of loads are failing, and it's lasted for 2 days.

Extensions with fewer than 10 loads in a week aren't rated. When an extension reaches Critical, store staff who can view reports and access your app receive an alert in the Shopify admin.

Check your extensions in the Dev Dashboard now so you can fix issues before merchants see them.

Learn what merchants will see

title: Merchant notes on store credit transactions
summary:
As of GraphQL Admin API version 2027-01, you can attach a merchant-only note when crediting or debiting a store credit account and read those notes on store credit transactions. Notes are optional, so existing integrations continue to work without changes or required updates.

What changed

  • StoreCreditAccountCreditInput and StoreCreditAccountDebitInput accept an optional note string.
  • StoreCreditAccountTransaction.note returns the stored note for credit, debit, and debit-revert transactions, or null when no note is set. Expiration transactions always return null.
  • Notes support up to 5,000 characters. Longer notes return a NOTE_TOO_LONG user error and the API doesn’t create the transaction.
  • Notes are for merchants only and aren't visible to customers. You can set a note when you create a transaction, but you can’t edit a note on an existing transaction.

Who's affected

This change applies to apps that manage store credit using GraphQL Admin API version 2027-01 or later. Versions 2026-10 and earlier don’t expose these fields.

Existing read_store_credit_account_transactions and write_store_credit_account_transactions access scopes and permission requirements still apply. No new scope is required.

What to do

You don’t need to change existing integrations. To start using notes:

  1. Target GraphQL Admin API version 2027-01 or later in your app.
  2. When you create a credit or debit, include note in the input.
  3. Select note on the returned StoreCreditAccountTransaction to read the stored value.
  4. Test in a dev store by creating a transaction with a note and verifying that the response includes the expected note string.

Related docs

  • storeCreditAccountCredit mutation reference
  • storeCreditAccountDebit mutation reference

title: orderCreate line items support custom IDs
summary:
The variantIdentifier field on orderCreate line items is now available in GraphQL Admin API version 2027-01 and later. Previously, it was only available in the unstable version. You can use it to identify a product variant by its ID or by a custom ID, such as a listing ID from another system that you store in a metafield. This is an additive change to the 2027-01 release candidate, so no action is required.

What changed

In version 2027-01, OrderCreateLineItemInput includes the variantIdentifier field. Provide exactly one of the following:

  • id: the global ID of the product variant.
  • customId: the namespace, key and value of an id metafield on the product variant. If you omit namespace, your app-reserved namespace is used.

Use variantIdentifier instead of variantId and productId. If a line item sets variantIdentifier together with either of those fields, then orderCreate returns a user error with the INVALID code.

To look up variants by custom ID, the store needs a metafield definition of type id for product variants, and your app must be able to read it. If the definition doesn't exist, then orderCreate returns an INVALID user error saying that the definition is required.

If no variant in the store matches an identifier, then orderCreate returns a user error with the VARIANT_IDENTIFIER_NOT_FOUND code for that line item, and doesn't create the order. Line items that use variantId work as before.

Who's affected

The change applies to apps that create orders with orderCreate. It's most useful for sales channels and integrations that identify products by an ID from an external system.

  • API version 2027-01 and later include variantIdentifier.
  • API version 2026-10 and earlier don't include it.
  • Apps that already use variantIdentifier on unstable can move to 2027-01 without changing their requests.

variantIdentifier needs no access scopes beyond those that orderCreate already requires. Custom ID lookups only find metafields that your app can read.

What to do

No action is required. To start using custom IDs on order line items:

  1. Check that the store has a metafield definition of type id for product variants, and that each variant stores its external ID in that metafield.
  2. Update your app to API version 2027-01.
  3. Pass variantIdentifier on each line item that you identify by custom ID:
mutation {
  orderCreate(order: {
    lineItems: [{
      variantIdentifier: {
        customId: { namespace: "custom", key: "listing_id", value: "LST-10045" }
      }
      quantity: 1
    }]
  }) {
    order { id lineItems(first: 1) { nodes { variant { id } } } }
    userErrors { field message code }
  }
}

This example creates an order for the variant whose custom.listing_id metafield is LST-10045. Replace the namespace, key and value with your own metafield definition and external ID, and add the other order fields that your app normally sends.

  1. Test in a development store. Create an order with a known custom ID and check that the line item refers to the expected variant. Then send an unknown value and check that userErrors returns VARIANT_IDENTIFIER_NOT_FOUND.

Why this matters

Until now, an app that knew a variant only by an external ID had two options. It could keep its own mapping from external IDs to Shopify variant IDs, or it could look up each variant with productVariantByIdentifier before calling orderCreate. Now you can pass the external ID in the same request that creates the order.

Related docs

  • Working with custom IDs
  • orderCreate mutation
  • OrderCreateLineItemInput reference

title: App security updates: IP allowlist is now required
summary:
On Oct 27 we recommended the IP allowlist. It is now required for every public app by November 20, or November 12 if you use bulk ops. An IP allowlist means a leaked token can't be used anywhere but your own servers. With the busiest weeks of the year for merchants almost here, we're asking for it now.

Action required

  • All public apps that call the Admin API: Turn on the IP allowlist by November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. With it on, your tokens only work from the addresses or networks you list, so a leaked token can't be used anywhere else. The IP allowlist is required for public apps. If you're on serverless or dynamic IPs, you'll need to allowlist by network with ASN support instead.

  • Bulk operations: Turn on the IP allowlist by November 12, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. After that date, bulk queries and mutations from public apps without an IP allowlist are blocked.

Also this week

  • Merchants can now see your app's security setup in Settings > Apps: expiring tokens and IP allowlist. After November 20, apps without an IP allowlist are flagged.
  • Find non-expiring tokens fast: filter your Dev Dashboard API logs by token type. And our Token Expiry FAQ answers the most common questions.
  • Network access testing in dev store previews: You can now test your network_access declarations before you release. It flags any site or server your app uses that you haven't declared yet. Test network access in dev store previews
  • Run app security checks in CI/CD. A new tutorial walks you through how to automatically scan your app for security issues.
  • Coming soon, access scopes for bulk operations: Bulk queries and bulk mutations will each need their own scope. If your app ran a bulk operation in the last 180 days, Shopify grants the scopes automatically. Once they're live, add them to your app config before your next deploy. We'll share the changelog with the scope names when ready.

If you miss a deadline

To protect merchant security, we'll begin enforcing IP allowlists starting in November. The timelines for expiring offline access tokens remain the same. In both cases, existing installs keep working until April 1, 2027:

| | IP allowlist | Expiring offline access tokens | | :

title: IP allowlists are now required for public apps
summary:
We're enhancing protection of merchants by adding IP allowlist configuration as a requirement for public apps. All public apps using bulk operations must configure an allowlist by November 12, 2026, and all other public apps must configure an allowlist by November 20, 2026.

If an app is not migrated by these dates:

  • November 12, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.: Bulk operations from public apps without an IP allowlist will fail to execute.
  • November 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET: Public apps without an IP allowlist will be delisted from the Shopify App Store and blocked from new installs.

What apps are affected

All public apps.

What apps are unaffected

  • Custom apps
  • Apps created by merchants either in the Dev Dashboard or in the admin

Why we're making this change

Leaked tokens can be used from any network location. IP allowlists reduce the impact of a credential leak by limiting the networks from which your app can invoke the Admin API.

What to do

Configure your app's allowed IPs in the Dev Dashboard:

  • If your app calls Shopify from static IP addresses, configure your IP allowlist based on static IPs or CIDR range.
  • If your app's egress IP addresses are dynamic, allow your hosting provider's ASNs and list the countries your app runs in.

For setup instructions, see Restrict API access with an IP allowlist.

What if my app makes Admin API calls from merchant infrastructure?

You should move as quickly as possible to an architecture that better limits exposure of Admin API tokens. You may submit a request for an extension to the deadlines above.

title: App IP allowlists now support apps with serverless hosting through ASNs
summary:
Apps without static IP addresses, such as apps on serverless platforms, can now add your hosting provider's autonomous system numbers (ASNs) to your app's IP allowlist in the Dev Dashboard.

What changed

The IP allowlist section of your app's Settings page now lets you allow either IP addresses or Networks (ASN). For networks, enter up to 10 ASNs and limit them to up to 10 countries. Test them against recent traffic, then turn on enforcement. Requests from outside your allowed networks fail with a 403 status code.

What to do

IP allowlists will soon be required for all public apps. Shopify strongly recommends all apps use an IP allowlist.

If your app calls Shopify from static IP addresses, keep allowing those addresses. If your app's egress IP addresses are dynamic, allow your hosting provider's ASNs and list the countries your app runs in.

For setup instructions, see Restrict API access with an IP allowlist.

title: Test app network access configuration on dev stores
summary:
You can now test your app's [network_access] settings on a dev store with the new network access testing feature preview. The preview helps you confirm you have the right networks listed, and find hosts and servers you missed.

What changed

When you create a dev store with the network_access_testing feature preview, you can confirm your network configuration behaves as expected:

  • Links to hosts that aren't in allowed_navigation_hosts show the exit warning, so you can ensure you're warning when appropriate and not showing exit warnings for trusted hosts.
  • The browser console warns when a storefront page loads from or sends requests to a server that isn't in allowed_sources. The preview only warns. It doesn't block anything.

Who's affected

Any app whose code links to or contacts external servers from a storefront can use this new testing option. Shopify recommends all apps configure these settings to avoid navigation warnings on merchant sites, and to help Shopify spot suspicious activity.

What to do

For step-by-step instructions and troubleshooting, follow the steps to test network access configuration on a dev store.

title: RETRY_DECLINED added to CustomerPaymentMethodRevocationReason
summary:
As of GraphQL Admin API version2027-01, CustomerPaymentMethod.revokedReason can return a new value: RETRY_DECLINED. Shopify uses this value when a subscription payment method is revoked because the payment processor has blocked any further retry attempts. On earlier API versions, these revocations continue to return TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.

If your app reads CustomerPaymentMethod.revokedReason using API version 2027-01, use RETRY_DECLINED to indicate to merchants and buyers that the processor has blocked further charges to the saved payment method and that a different payment method is required.

The customer_payment_methods/revoke webhook payload is unchanged. After receiving the webhook, query CustomerPaymentMethod.revokedReason to determine whether the payment method was revoked because of RETRY_DECLINED or TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.

The customer_payment_methods/revoke webhook payload is unchanged. After receiving the webhook, query CustomerPaymentMethod.revokedReason to determine whether the payment method was revoked because of RETRY_DECLINED or TOO_MANY_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.

title: currententrychange now returns the previous page in event.from for customer account full-page extensions
summary:
Starting in API version 2027-01, in customer account full-page extensions the Navigation API currententrychange event sets event.from to the page the customer navigated away from, instead of the page they navigated to. This is a breaking change for customer account full-page extensions that read the new page from event.from. Update them to read shopify.navigation.currentEntry before you move them to 2027-01.

What changed

In customer account full-page extensions (customer-account.page.render and customer-account.order.page.render), currententrychange passes a NavigationCurrentEntryChangeEvent whose from property is documented as the previous history entry. In API version 2026-10 and earlier, from is the new entry instead, the same value as shopify.navigation.currentEntry. Starting in 2027-01, from is the previous entry.

Who's affected

Full-page extensions on API version 2027-01 or later that use event.from to find the page the customer navigated to are affected.

Extensions on 2026-10 and earlier aren't affected, because their behavior doesn't change. Extensions that read shopify.navigation.currentEntry, including extensions that use the useNavigationCurrentEntry hook, aren't affected on any version.

Breaking changes and migrations

On 2027-01, code that reads the new page from event.from.url gets the previous page's URL instead. For example, an extension that chooses which route to render from event.from keeps showing the previous route after each navigation.

Replace those reads with shopify.navigation.currentEntry.url.

Before:

shopify.navigation.addEventListener('currententrychange', (event) => {
  setPath(new URL(event.from.url).pathname);
});

After:

shopify.navigation.addEventListener('currententrychange', () => {
  setPath(new URL(shopify.navigation.currentEntry.url).pathname);
});

The updated code works on API version 2025-10 and later, so you can make the change before you update your API version.

Action required

Before you update a customer account full-page extension to 2027-01, update every currententrychange handler that reads the new page from event.from. To confirm the update, navigate between two routes in your extension and check that each navigation shows the page you navigated to.

Related docs

  • Navigation API reference for customer account UI extensions
